acknowledge.text: A quiet moment. Those are worth having.
Things feel settled right now. Nothing needs to happen.
Deeply calm. Let yourself stay here a while.
This is a good, still place to be.

understand.text: Calm often goes unnoticed, because nothing is asking for attention. Noticing it can help you find your way back on busier days.
Many people find calm easier to return to once they know what it feels like in their body.

options.title: Notice where it lives
options.text: Where do you feel this calm? Your shoulders, your breath, your hands? Just notice.
options.why: Knowing how calm feels in your body can give you something to look for later.

options.title: What got you here?
options.text: What helped you arrive at this feeling today?
options.why: Knowing what brings you calm can make it easier to find on a busier day.
options.prompt: What helped me feel calm today:

options.title: A note for a tense day
options.text: Write to yourself for a day when things feel tight: what does calm feel like, and what helped?
options.why: On a tense day, a reminder from a calm you can be easier to trust.

options.title: Do one thing slowly
options.text: Make a drink, water a plant, tidy one shelf. Slowly, because you can.
options.why: Doing something slowly on purpose can help calm last a little longer.

options.title: A gentle hello
options.text: Send a kind message to someone you haven't heard from in a while.
options.why: Calm moments are often good ones for reaching out without pressure.

options.title: Just listen
options.text: Put on a calm sound and do nothing else for a little while.
options.why: Giving yourself permission to do nothing is a way of resting properly.

options.title: A question for a quiet moment
options.text: What matters to you that's easy to forget on busy days?
options.why: Quiet moments are often when the important things are easiest to hear.
